# Rules & strategy

Curated in [`data/rules.toml`](../data/rules.toml) — long form in [RULES.md](../RULES.md). Targets are linked to rules automatically (the rule's `match` patterns) or by `rules = [...]` on the target.

- **PC** — Best graphics — but Steam sales only, no physical PC games. Owning a game on Steam lowers the priority of the disc.
- **Nintendo** — Best physical line-up. First choice for JRPGs and for anything with a real Switch cart.
- **PlayStation** — Exclusives plus multiplatform games worth having on disc. Fill the collection while discs are still made — the next PlayStation is probably not being bought.
- **Xbox** — Shooter console (full Call of Duty + Battlefield runs) and Microsoft first-party on disc for the Disc-to-Digital licence — even for games released elsewhere.

## General

### Physical first `physical-first`

Physical first. Digital only when there is no other option.

_Why:_ The collection is about owning discs and carts; digital purchases are a fallback, not a goal.

### PC → Nintendo → PS/Xbox `platform-priority`

Platform order: PC (best graphics) → Nintendo (best physical line-up) → whatever is still exclusive on PlayStation or Xbox.

_Why:_ Each game is bought once, on the platform where it plays or collects best.

### One copy, newest gen `one-copy-newest-gen`

One copy per game. For cross-gen releases take the newest-gen version.

_Why:_ Avoids double-buying; the newest pressing plays on current hardware and usually runs best.

_Precedents:_ Battlefield Hardline on Xbox One, not 360

### Compilations count `compilations-count`

Compilations and remasters on a newer gen replace the originals and count as owning their games.

_Why:_ No need to hunt older discs when a newer disc contains the same games.

_Precedents:_ MW Trilogy → CoD 4 / MW2 / MW3 · MCC → Halo CE–4 · God of War Collection → GoW I + II · Gears UE → Gears of War · Year One → State of Decay

### Gaps bought used `used-for-gaps`

Gaps in older generations are mostly bought used.

_Why:_ Older discs are cheap and plentiful used; new copies are often gone or overpriced.

### Game-Key Card ≠ physical `gkc-not-physical`

A Switch 2 Game-Key Card does not count as physical for non-JRPGs → take the PlayStation disc. JRPGs whose only Switch version is a Game-Key Card → case by case.

_Why:_ A Game-Key Card is only a download licence in a box; the disc is the real physical copy.

_Precedents:_ Pragmata, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Full Metal Schoolgirl → PS5 · Bravely Default HD Remaster, Brigandine Abyss, Granblue Fantasy: Relink bought as GKC (JRPGs)
